author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand sits down with Jim Gale to explore what it actually looks like to live completely off the grid through regenerative farming, growing his own food and generating free electricity entirely independent of the system. Jim opens up about the day government agents showed up at his property and how he turned the encounter into a powerful demonstration of why compliance with government control leads to the collapse of personal sovereignty and self sufficiency. Russell and Jim make the case that true freedom begins with breaking dependence on the systems designed to keep you powerless.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to the case of the Newburgh Four where Federal Judge Colleen McMahon ordered the release of three men after heavily criticising the FBI and their informant for radicalising vulnerable and easily manipulated individuals into participating in a completely fabricated synagogue and airplane bombing plot. Russell asks the question that nobody in mainstream media will touch — if the FBI was willing to manufacture an entire terror plot from scratch to secure arrests, what else have they orchestrated and what does that reveal about the true state of American democracy and the institutions trusted to protect it.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to a compilation of Keir Starmer's most bizarre and uncomfortable public moments and genuinely cannot make sense of what he is watching. From stumbling through classroom visits to struggling to string together a coherent sentence Russell questions how someone this awkward and deeply strange ended up leading one of the world's most prominent democracies. Russell does not hold back in pointing out just how unsettling Starmer's behavior is and what it reveals about the complete absence of authentic leadership at the top of British politics.
